source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source_reported_historical_synonyms: Mimosa quadrivalvis var. platycarpa (A. Gray) Barneby

morphology_source_reported.leaves: Usually 4–5 pinna pairs, leaflets sensitive to touch/night movement
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Petals united nearly halfway; conspicuous pink filaments
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Flattened mature fruit 4–6 mm wide, 3–6 times wider than thick [key]; lower stems rounded or five-sided [key]
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: Flattened rather than nearly four-sided mature pods distinguish from M. latidens

habitat_source_reported: Rocky limestone slopes, occasionally sandy soils
cautions: Historical M. quadrivalvis variety relationship requires taxonomic reconciliation
Source morphology has not been independently corroborated or approved for identification scoring
Regional habitat and distribution do not establish Hays County nativity
